bank.q: Consider the following statements about the decline of legislative scrutiny:
s: Sitting days have fallen from around 127 a year in the 1950s to under 70.
Committee referral of Bills fell to around 16% in the 17th Lok Sabha.
Average standing committee attendance was around 49% between 2009 and 2014.
bank.e: All three are correct, and together they describe the same institutional problem from three angles — less time, less referral, less participation.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (holding):
pairs: 1. No immunity from bribery prosecution for a vote or speech
2. A Speaker cannot indefinitely sit on anti-defection petitions
3. The Speaker's decision is subject to judicial review
4. Punishment by the House does not extend to future disqualification
bank.e: Kihoto on reviewability, Sita Soren on bribery, Raja Ram Pal on the limits of punishment, and Padi Kaushik Reddy on Speaker inaction.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT correct?
o: The anti-defection law applies to an MLA cross-voting in a Rajya Sabha election
The 91st Amendment removed the split defence from the Tenth Schedule
The Speaker certifies a Bill as a Money Bill under Article 110
There was no Deputy Speaker throughout the 17th Lok Sabha
bank.e: A Rajya Sabha election is not a proceeding of the Assembly, so the Tenth Schedule does not apply — the largest acknowledged gap in the anti-defection regime.

bank.as: India is among only six countries that legally compel legislators to vote as their party directs.
bank.rs: The Tenth Schedule makes voting or abstaining contrary to a party direction a ground for disqualification.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion. The United States and United Kingdom rely on internal party sanctions alone.

s: Article 249 belongs exclusively to the Rajya Sabha.
Money Bill certification belongs exclusively to the Lok Sabha Speaker.
No-confidence motions may be moved in either House.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. No-confidence motions lie only in the Lok Sabha, because the Council of Ministers is responsible to that House alone.

bank.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a reform with the body that recommended it?
o: Confining whips to confidence votes and money bills — 170th Law Commission
A three-month anti-defection deadline — Halim Committee
bank.e: The 170th Law Commission, endorsed by the NCRWC. Privileges codification came from the Lok Sabha Privileges Committee, the three-month deadline from Keisham Meghachandra Singh, and internal party democracy from the Second ARC.

bank.q: All of the following weaken the office of Speaker EXCEPT:
o: The absence of a deadline for anti-defection rulings
Removal requiring a majority of all the then members
Election by consensus with the Opposition
bank.e: Consensus election is a proposed reform, drawn from the Halim Committee and the 170th Law Commission.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about office of profit:
s: The Constitution does not define the term.
Conflict of interest is described as the crucial factor in the Swapan Roy tests.
Prestige alone can bring an office within the bar.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Hedge v. Karnataka requires pecuniary advantage — prestige alone is insufficient.

bank.q: Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
items: Sita Soren overturns the bribery immunity
The 91st Amendment removes the split defence
bank.e: Tenth Schedule (1985) → Kihoto Hollohan (1992) → 91st Amendment (2003) → Sita Soren (2024).

bank.as: The Rajya Sabha is described as a chamber of second thought rather than a speed breaker.
bank.rs: It never dissolves, changes composition slowly, and includes twelve nominated members chosen for distinction in literature, science, art and social service.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — continuity and expertise are precisely what allow revision rather than obstruction.
